Senses.Explanation: This stock public-interview question asks what the Way is. Nanquan answers Zhaozhou, ‘the ordinary mind is the Way’ (平常心是道); when Zhaozhou asks whether one can head toward it, Nanquan says that intending to head toward it departs from it (擬向即乖). Other records preserve unlike answers without a single harmonizing gloss: ‘white clouds cover the green peaks; bees and butterflies love the courtyard flowers’ (白雲覆青嶂，蜂蝶戀庭華), ‘every household's gate opens onto Chang'an’ (家家門口通長安), and ‘what is sweet is licorice’ (甜底是甘草). Panshan Baoji merely rebuffs the question and sends the monk away. In a longer written questionnaire, the answer begins ‘unobstructed is the Way’ (無礙是道). Zhaozhou's record also makes the ordinary road-word audible: Zhaozhou first answers ‘the one outside the wall’ (墻外底); when the monk says he means the great Way, the answer is ‘the great road runs through Chang'an’ (大道透長安). The dictionary therefore retains the direct question and its observable public-interview role; the mutually different recorded answers are not converted into an interpretive menu.
Senses.Note: Capitalize “Way” when the exchange distinguishes it from an ordinary road, but translate the road wordplay explicitly where it occurs.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南泉因趙州問。如何是道。泉云。平常心是道。州云。還可趣向否。泉云。擬向即乖。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Gateless Barrier (無門關) records Zhaozhou Congshen as the exact questioner who asks Nanquan Puyuan what the Way is; Wumen Huikai is the later case compiler.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是道。師曰。白雲覆青嶂。蜂蝶戀庭華。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Tianzhu Chonghui section: an unnamed questioner asks ‘What is the Way?’ Tianzhu answers with clouds, peaks, bees, and flowers without repeating the headword; the questioner is the exact token speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一問。如何是道。何以修之。為復必須修成。為復不假功用。答。無礙是道。覺妄是修。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Sikong Benjing's written question-and-answer sequence. An unnamed questioner asks what the Way is and how it is cultivated; Sikong Benjing supplies the answer. The six-rung ladder does not identify the questioner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是道。師便咄。僧曰。學人未領旨。師曰。去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Panshan Baoji section. An unnamed monk asks, 'What is the Way?'; Panshan responds first with a rebuff and then with 'go.' The six-rung ladder and parallel forms do not name the monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是道。師曰。墻外底。曰。不問這箇。師曰。你問那箇。曰。大道。師曰。大道透長安。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Zhaozhou Congshen section. An unnamed monk asks 'What is the Way?' and then distinguishes the great Way from the road outside the wall; Zhaozhou answers. The six-rung ladder does not name the monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是道？師云：家家門口通長安。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jianzhong Jingguo Continuation of the Lamp Record (建中靖國續燈錄), Luohan section: an unnamed questioner asks ‘What is the Way?’ Luohan says every household gate opens onto Chang'an without repeating the headword; the questioner is the exact token speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是道？師云：甜底是甘草。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jianzhong Jingguo Continuation of the Lamp Record (建中靖國續燈錄), in Zhimen Guangzuo's record, preserves an unnamed questioner asking what the Way is and Zhimen answering that the sweet thing is licorice. The six-rung ladder does not identify the questioner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂舉。李翱相公問藥山。如何是道。山指天復指淨缾云。會麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Extended Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄) records Hongzhi Zhengjue raising the older exchange in which Li Ao is the exact questioner and Yaoshan Weiyan responds by pointing to the sky and then a clean bottle.
